title: Enhancement: PDDF Support Multiple PSU Thermals
author: antonio-nexthop
body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

Medium

### Description of the enhancement

Currently PDDF supports one thermal sensor per PSU. This enhancement adds support to parse, create sysfs paths and display temperatures for all three.

PDDF supports one thermal sensor per PSU, for example:
- https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/blob/d9c7bbbfd0b44c998b42d3277a1c9758ddc1cd70/platform/pddf/platform-api-pddf-base/sonic_platform_pddf_base/pddf_psu.py#L57
- https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/blob/d9c7bbbfd0b44c998b42d3277a1c9758ddc1cd70/platform/pddf/platform-api-pddf-base/sonic_platform_pddf_base/pddf_thermal.py#L77
- https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/blob/d9c7bbbfd0b44c998b42d3277a1c9758ddc1cd70/platform/pddf/i2c/modules/include/pddf_psu_driver.h#L36-L37
- https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/blob/d9c7bbbfd0b44c998b42d3277a1c9758ddc1cd70/platform/pddf/i2c/modules/psu/driver/pddf_psu_driver.c#L95-L99
- https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/blob/d9c7bbbfd0b44c998b42d3277a1c9758ddc1cd70/platform/pddf/i2c/modules/psu/driver/pddf_psu_api.c#L242-L243


### Current Behavior

PDDF supports one thermal sensor per PSU.

### Proposed Behavior

PDDF supports a system with up to three thermal sensors per PSU.

comments.body:
> Can you provide the UT log for check ? Did you verify if it still work fine with single PSU thermal platform as well ?
> 
> Geans

Thank you for the comment Geans!

Here is the sample output of `show plat temp` on our NH-4010 system using only 1 PSU Thermal
```
admin@xxxx150-dut:~$ show plat temp
                Sensor    Temperature    High TH    Low TH    Crit High TH    Crit Low TH    Warning          Timestamp
----------------------  -------------  ---------  --------  --------------  -------------  ---------  -----------------
          ASIC Diode 0         42.875      120.0       N/A           127.0            N/A      False  20250717 21:18:37
          ASIC Diode 1          41.75      120.0       N/A           127.0            N/A      False  20250717 21:18:37
              ASIC Max          40.03       95.0       N/A           110.0            N/A      False  20250717 21:18:37
              ASIC Min         23.192       95.0       N/A           110.0            N/A      False  20250717 21:18:37
        Chassis Intake           23.0       45.0       N/A            65.0            N/A      False  20250717 21:18:37
            PSU1_TEMP1         26.406       70.0       N/A             N/A            N/A      False  20250717 21:18:37
            PSU2_TEMP1         29.593       70.0       N/A             N/A            N/A      False  20250717 21:18:37
          PSU 1 Intake         22.938      100.0       N/A           105.0            N/A      False  20250717 21:18:37
          PSU 2 Intake         23.313      100.0       N/A           105.0            N/A      False  20250717 21:18:37
Switch Card Lower Rear         26.813      100.0       N/A           105.0            N/A      False  20250717 21:18:37
...
...
...
```
To ensure compatibility with single PSU thermal platform, we check the `pddf-device.json` to see how many PSU Thermals are defined. Further, SysFS paths are created only if the respective `psu_temp*_input` or `psu_temp*_high_threshold` are defined. 

For example on our system with 1 PSU thermal ([sample pddf-device.json](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21305175/pddf-device.json), note there is only 1 `psu_temp*_input` and `psu_temp*_high_threshold`) the SysFS paths would look like:
```
...
/sys/kernel/pddf/devices/psu/i2c/psu_temp_high_thresh_bitmap
/sys/devices/pci0000:00/0000:00:02.2/0000:04:00.0/i2c-19/i2c-87/87-0058/psu_temp1_high_threshold
/sys/devices/pci0000:00/0000:00:02.2/0000:04:00.0/i2c-19/i2c-87/87-0058/psu_temp1_input
/sys/devices/pci0000:00/0000:00:02.2/0000:04:00.0/i2c-19/i2c-88/88-0058/psu_temp1_high_threshold
/sys/devices/pci0000:00/0000:00:02.2/0000:04:00.0/i2c-19/i2c-88/88-0058/psu_temp1_input
...
```
